CVE-2024-3651.d48c424fd02576a57ed1407e98850aa6af4aabb1:
build(deps): clear the open security alerts across test requirements and uv.lock (#5271)

* build(deps): bump Pygments to 2.20.0 in richconsole tests

Fixes GHSA-5239-wwwm-4pmq, a regular expression denial of service in
the GUID matching regex.

* build(deps): bump bleach to 6.4.0 in dev-requirements

Fixes GHSA-gj48-438w-jh9v, where clean() and Cleaner() fail to sanitize
dangerous URI schemes in allowed formaction attributes, and
GHSA-8rfp-98v4-mmr6, where URI sanitization allows disallowed schemes
with Unicode above U+00A0 in the output.

* build(deps): bump idna to 3.15 across test requirements

Fixes GHSA-65pc-fj4g-8rjx, where specially crafted input to
idna.encode() bypasses the CVE-2024-3651 fix.

* build(deps): bump sqlparse to 0.6.0 in django tests

Fixes six advisories, the most severe being GHSA-f2ff-p2ww-7p4p
(quadratic denial of service in group_comments), GHSA-prg7-hcfm-mfcr
(ReDoS on dollar-quoted SQL literals) and GHSA-pwgv-4x5q-6m9f (CPU
exhaustion in TokenList.__init__ before the depth and token caps apply).

* build(deps): bump cryptography to 49.0.0 in botocore tests

Fixes five advisories, including GHSA-jwv3-5hgf-82ww (exponential path
building from duplicate self-signed intermediates), GHSA-537c-gmf6-5ccf
and GHSA-79v4-65xg-pq4g (vulnerable OpenSSL bundled in the wheels), and
GHSA-r6ph-v2qm-q3c2 (missing subgroup validation for SECT curves).

cffi moves to 2.0.0 because cryptography 49.0.0 requires it.

* build(deps): bump urllib3 to 2.8.0 where botocore does not cap it

Fixes eight advisories, the most severe being GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77 (HTTPS
proxy TLS configuration ignored or overridden), GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw
(unbounded chunk-size line buffered into memory) and GHSA-qccp-gfcp-xxvc
(sensitive headers forwarded across origins on proxied redirects).

botocore test-requirements-0.txt and -2.txt and the boto3sqs test
requirements stay on urllib3 1.26.19. The botocore releases they pin
(1.31.80, 1.32.4 and 1.34.44) require urllib3<2.1, and no advisory here
has a fix in the 1.x series, so moving them would mean moving botocore
and changing what those environments test.

* build(deps): bump Werkzeug to 3.1.9 outside the flask matrix

Fixes GHSA-g6x2-hccm-hh4m and the earlier safe_join() advisories
GHSA-29vq-49wr-vm6x, GHSA-87hc-h4r5-73f7 and GHSA-hgf8-39gv-g3f2, which
let Windows special device names through.

The flask test requirements keep their current Werkzeug pins. tox.ini
documents environments 0 and 1 as Werkzeug <3.0.0 and environment 2 as
the 3.0.x band, and every remaining advisory is first fixed in 3.1.x, so
there is no in-band fix for those three files.

* build(deps): bump anyio to 4.14.2 in httpx test-requirements-1

Fixes GHSA-82r6-8w77-94w6 (IDNA 2003 host name encoding in TLSStream
enabling TLS certificate spoofing), GHSA-3w57-8xmc-8v26 (run_process
and open_process ignore extra_groups) and GHSA-5p39-cfhj-2xmp (process
pool workers block on undrained stderr).

test-requirements-0.txt keeps anyio 3.7.1. tox.ini describes that
environment as httpx>=0.18.0,<0.19.0, and anyio 4.x does not resolve
against that httpx.

* build(deps): bump Flask in the files that are not pinned by the matrix

The aiohttp-client and click test requirements use Flask only as a test
server, so they move to 3.1.3 and fix GHSA-68rp-wp8r-4726, where the
session does not add a Vary: Cookie header when accessed in some ways.
itsdangerous and blinker move because Flask 3.1.3 requires them.

flask test-requirements-1.txt moves 2.2.0 to 2.2.5, which stays inside
the 2.2 series that tox.ini assigns to that environment and fixes
GHSA-m2qf-hxjv-5gpq, a possible disclosure of the permanent session
cookie.

test-requirements-0.txt stays on Flask 2.1.3 and test-requirements-2.txt
on 3.0.2. tox.ini assigns those environments the 2.1 and 3.0 series, and
neither advisory has a fix inside them.

* build(deps): bump Django to the latest patch of each tested series

test-requirements-2.txt moves 4.2.17 to 4.2.30, the last 4.2 release,
clearing everything from GHSA-qcgg-j2x8-h9g8 up to GHSA-mvfq-ggxm-9mc5
that has a 4.2 fix, including the critical SQL injection via the
_connector keyword argument, GHSA-frmv-pr5f-9mcr.

test-requirements-3.txt moves 5.2.11 to 5.2.17.

The docker tests are not part of the Django version matrix, so they move
from 4.2.30 to 5.2.17. Django 4.2 is past end of extended support, so
the advisories still open against it have no 4.2 fix at all. The test
only uses re_path, settings.configure and the test Client, which are
unchanged across that range.

test-requirements-0.txt and -1.txt keep Django 2.2.28 and 3.2.25. tox.ini
assigns them the 2.x and 3.x series and both are long past end of life,
so no fix exists within them.

* build(deps): bump httpx2 to 2.12.0 in httpx tests

Fixes GHSA-8xx6-hgc6-gc2m (streaming response decompression does not
bound peak memory), GHSA-h4x7-gw46-3wm6 (multipart part header
injection) and GHSA-pf96-p4fj-6566 (conflicting Content-Length and
Transfer-Encoding headers can be auto-generated).

* build(deps): bump mysql-connector-python to 9.1.0

Fixes GHSA-hgjp-83m4-h4fj, a connector takeover vulnerability.

mysql test-requirements-1.txt moves from 9.0.0 to 9.1.0, which steps one
minor past the ~=9.0.0 that tox.ini records for that environment, and
docs-requirements.txt moves from ~=8.0 to ~=9.1.

Two files keep an 8.x pin. mysql test-requirements-0.txt is the 8.x entry
of the matrix tox.ini documents, and the fix is first available in 9.1.0.
The docker tests keep 8.3.0 because 9.1.0 makes five sqlalchemy tests in
sqlalchemy_tests/test_mysql.py fail: the span name drops to SELECT from
SELECT opentelemetry-tests, so the database name is no longer reaching
the span. That is a behaviour change in the instrumentation rather than a
stale expectation, so it needs its own investigation.

* build(deps): bump pymongo to 4.18.2

Fixes GHSA-v4x9-3549-crwv (heap out-of-bounds write via signed size
overflow in BSON document encoding), GHSA-vp6j-j7w5-5xjj (host injection
in connection string parsing), GHSA-qx36-8mw2-4r3x (forced Unix domain
socket connection via a .sock KMS endpoint) and GHSA-8fvv-fgr5-f8ch
(inexact file ID match in GridFS delete methods).

dnspython moves because pymongo 4.18.2 requires it.

* build(deps): widen starlette to ~=1.3.1 in docs-requirements

Fixes GHSA-82w8-qh3p-5jfq (request.form() limits silently ignored for
application/x-www-form-urlencoded), GHSA-wqp7-x3pw-xc5r (SSRF and NTLM
credential theft via UNC paths in StaticFiles) and the remaining open
starlette advisories, none of which has a fix inside the ~=0.50 range
this file pinned.

* build(deps): bump the vulnerable pins in the uv-generated test requirements

Covers anyio 4.14.2 (GHSA-82r6-8w77-94w6, GHSA-3w57-8xmc-8v26,
GHSA-5p39-cfhj-2xmp), urllib3 2.8.0 (GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77 and the rest of
the open urllib3 set), kafka-python 2.3.2 (GHSA-2jcm-hq8r-84wx and
GHSA-m3px-q5gj-j9x7) and multidict 6.9.1 (GHSA-54p9-h82j-f925).

The matching floors in the test-requirements.in files move with them, so
a later regeneration cannot drop back below a fix.

These files are edited in place rather than regenerated. Regenerating
fastapi test-requirements.latest.txt from its current .in file replaces
fastapi 0.137.2 with 0.119.1 and starlette 1.3.1 with 0.48.0, because
the .in file still asks for fastapi~=0.119.1. That would reintroduce the
starlette advisories this PR is clearing, so the generated files have
been left otherwise untouched.

fastapi test-requirements.oldest.txt keeps starlette 0.48.0. It pins
fastapi 0.119.1, which requires starlette<0.49.0, and the first starlette
fix is 0.49.1.

* build(deps): upgrade the vulnerable packages in uv.lock

Moves aiohttp to 3.14.5, anyio to 4.14.2, Django to 5.2.18 and 6.1.2,
mcp to 1.30.0, multidict to 6.9.1, pyasn1 to 0.6.5, PyJWT to 2.15.1,
pymongo to 4.18.3 and 4.19.0, tornado to 6.5.10 and 6.6, urllib3 to
2.8.0, uv to 0.13.6, virtualenv to 21.15.1, WebOb to 1.8.11 and
Werkzeug to 3.1.9.

Two entries cannot reach a fixed release:

- setuptools stays at 81.0.0. pyramid 2.1, its latest release, requires
  setuptools<82, and the advisories are first fixed in 83.0.0. This is
  the same cap that test-constraints.txt and docs-requirements.txt
  already record for cassandra-driver and pyramid.
- filelock resolves to 4.1.0 on Python 3.10 and 4.2.4 elsewhere. The fix
  is in 4.2.1, which requires Python 3.11 or newer.

uv lock --check passes against pyproject.toml.

GHSA-29vq-49wr-vm6x, GHSA-87hc-h4r5-73f7 and GHSA-hgf8-39gv-g3f2, which
let Windows special device names through.

The flask test requirements keep their current Werkzeug pins. tox.ini
documents environments 0 and 1 as Werkzeug <3.0.0 and environment 2 as
the 3.0.x band, and every remaining advisory is first fixed in 3.1.x, so
there is no in-band fix for those three files.

* build(deps): bump anyio to 4.14.2 in httpx test-requirements-1

Fixes GHSA-82r6-8w77-94w6 (IDNA 2003 host name encoding in TLSStream
enabling TLS certificate spoofing), GHSA-3w57-8xmc-8v26 (run_process
and open_process ignore extra_groups) and GHSA-5p39-cfhj-2xmp (process
pool workers block on undrained stderr).

test-requirements-0.txt keeps anyio 3.7.1. tox.ini describes that
environment as httpx>=0.18.0,<0.19.0, and anyio 4.x does not resolve
against that httpx.

* build(deps): bump Flask in the files that are not pinned by the matrix

The aiohttp-client and click test requirements use Flask only as a test
server, so they move to 3.1.3 and fix GHSA-68rp-wp8r-4726, where the
session does not add a Vary: Cookie header when accessed in some ways.
itsdangerous and blinker move because Flask 3.1.3 requires them.

flask test-requirements-1.txt moves 2.2.0 to 2.2.5, which stays inside
the 2.2 series that tox.ini assigns to that environment and fixes
GHSA-m2qf-hxjv-5gpq, a possible disclosure of the permanent session
cookie.

test-requirements-0.txt stays on Flask 2.1.3 and test-requirements-2.txt
on 3.0.2. tox.ini assigns those environments the 2.1 and 3.0 series, and
neither advisory has a fix inside them.

* build(deps): bump Django to the latest patch of each tested series

test-requirements-2.txt moves 4.2.17 to 4.2.30, the last 4.2 release,
clearing everything from GHSA-qcgg-j2x8-h9g8 up to GHSA-mvfq-ggxm-9mc5
that has a 4.2 fix, including the critical SQL injection via the
_connector keyword argument, GHSA-frmv-pr5f-9mcr.

test-requirements-3.txt moves 5.2.11 to 5.2.17.

The docker tests are not part of the Django version matrix, so they move
from 4.2.30 to 5.2.17. Django 4.2 is past end of extended support, so
the advisories still open against it have no 4.2 fix at all. The test
only uses re_path, settings.configure and the test Client, which are
unchanged across that range.

test-requirements-0.txt and -1.txt keep Django 2.2.28 and 3.2.25. tox.ini
assigns them the 2.x and 3.x series and both are long past end of life,
so no fix exists within them.

* build(deps): bump httpx2 to 2.12.0 in httpx tests

Fixes GHSA-8xx6-hgc6-gc2m (streaming response decompression does not
bound peak memory), GHSA-h4x7-gw46-3wm6 (multipart part header
injection) and GHSA-pf96-p4fj-6566 (conflicting Content-Length and
Transfer-Encoding headers can be auto-generated).

* build(deps): bump mysql-connector-python to 9.1.0

Fixes GHSA-hgjp-83m4-h4fj, a connector takeover vulnerability.

mysql test-requirements-1.txt moves from 9.0.0 to 9.1.0, which steps one
minor past the ~=9.0.0 that tox.ini records for that environment, and
docs-requirements.txt moves from ~=8.0 to ~=9.1.

Two files keep an 8.x pin. mysql test-requirements-0.txt is the 8.x entry
of the matrix tox.ini documents, and the fix is first available in 9.1.0.
The docker tests keep 8.3.0 because 9.1.0 makes five sqlalchemy tests in
sqlalchemy_tests/test_mysql.py fail: the span name drops to SELECT from
SELECT opentelemetry-tests, so the database name is no longer reaching
the span. That is a behaviour change in the instrumentation rather than a
stale expectation, so it needs its own investigation.

* build(deps): bump pymongo to 4.18.2

Fixes GHSA-v4x9-3549-crwv (heap out-of-bounds write via signed size
overflow in BSON document encoding), GHSA-vp6j-j7w5-5xjj (host injection
in connection string parsing), GHSA-qx36-8mw2-4r3x (forced Unix domain
socket connection via a .sock KMS endpoint) and GHSA-8fvv-fgr5-f8ch
(inexact file ID match in GridFS delete methods).

dnspython moves because pymongo 4.18.2 requires it.

* build(deps): widen starlette to ~=1.3.1 in docs-requirements

Fixes GHSA-82w8-qh3p-5jfq (request.form() limits silently ignored for
application/x-www-form-urlencoded), GHSA-wqp7-x3pw-xc5r (SSRF and NTLM
credential theft via UNC paths in StaticFiles) and the remaining open
starlette advisories, none of which has a fix inside the ~=0.50 range
this file pinned.

* build(deps): bump the vulnerable pins in the uv-generated test requirements

Covers anyio 4.14.2 (GHSA-82r6-8w77-94w6, GHSA-3w57-8xmc-8v26,
GHSA-5p39-cfhj-2xmp), urllib3 2.8.0 (GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77 and the rest of
the open urllib3 set), kafka-python 2.3.2 (GHSA-2jcm-hq8r-84wx and
GHSA-m3px-q5gj-j9x7) and multidict 6.9.1 (GHSA-54p9-h82j-f925).

The matching floors in the test-requirements.in files move with them, so
a later regeneration cannot drop back below a fix.

These files are edited in place rather than regenerated. Regenerating
fastapi test-requirements.latest.txt from its current .in file replaces
fastapi 0.137.2 with 0.119.1 and starlette 1.3.1 with 0.48.0, because
the .in file still asks for fastapi~=0.119.1. That would reintroduce the
starlette advisories this PR is clearing, so the generated files have
been left otherwise untouched.

fastapi test-requirements.oldest.txt keeps starlette 0.48.0. It pins
fastapi 0.119.1, which requires starlette<0.49.0, and the first starlette
fix is 0.49.1.

* build(deps): upgrade the vulnerable packages in uv.lock

Moves aiohttp to 3.14.5, anyio to 4.14.2, Django to 5.2.18 and 6.1.2,
mcp to 1.30.0, multidict to 6.9.1, pyasn1 to 0.6.5, PyJWT to 2.15.1,
pymongo to 4.18.3 and 4.19.0, tornado to 6.5.10 and 6.6, urllib3 to
2.8.0, uv to 0.13.6, virtualenv to 21.15.1, WebOb to 1.8.11 and
Werkzeug to 3.1.9.

Two entries cannot reach a fixed release:

- setuptools stays at 81.0.0. pyramid 2.1, its latest release, requires
  setuptools<82, and the advisories are first fixed in 83.0.0. This is
  the same cap that test-constraints.txt and docs-requirements.txt
  already record for cassandra-driver and pyramid.
- filelock resolves to 4.1.0 on Python 3.10 and 4.2.4 elsewhere. The fix
  is in 4.2.1, which requires Python 3.11 or newer.

uv lock --check passes against pyproject.toml.

* build(deps): bump Werkzeug to 3.1.9 outside the flask matrix

Fixes GHSA-g6x2-hccm-hh4m and the earlier safe_join() advisories
GHSA-29vq-49wr-vm6x, GHSA-87hc-h4r5-73f7 and GHSA-hgf8-39gv-g3f2, which
let Windows special device names through.

The flask test requirements keep their current Werkzeug pins. tox.ini
documents environments 0 and 1 as Werkzeug <3.0.0 and environment 2 as
the 3.0.x band, and every remaining advisory is first fixed in 3.1.x, so
there is no in-band fix for those three files.

* build(deps): bump anyio to 4.14.2 in httpx test-requirements-1

Fixes GHSA-82r6-8w77-94w6 (IDNA 2003 host name encoding in TLSStream
enabling TLS certificate spoofing), GHSA-3w57-8xmc-8v26 (run_process
and open_process ignore extra_groups) and GHSA-5p39-cfhj-2xmp (process

test-requirements-0.txt keeps anyio 3.7.1. tox.ini describes that

session does not add a Vary: Cookie header when accessed in some ways.

GHSA-m2qf-hxjv-5gpq, a possible disclosure of the permanent session
cookie.

test-requirements-0.txt stays on Flask 2.1.3 and test-requirements-2.txt

neither advisory has a fix inside them.

the advisories still open against it have no 4.2 fix at all. The test
only uses re_path, settings.configure and the test Client, which are
unchanged across that range.

test-requirements-0.txt and -1.txt keep Django 2.2.28 and 3.2.25. tox.ini
assigns them the 2.x and 3.x series and both are long past end of life,
so no fix exists within them.

* build(deps): bump httpx2 to 2.12.0 in httpx tests

Fixes GHSA-8xx6-hgc6-gc2m (streaming response decompression does not
bound peak memory), GHSA-h4x7-gw46-3wm6 (multipart part header
injection) and GHSA-pf96-p4fj-6566 (conflicting Content-Length and
Transfer-Encoding headers can be auto-generated).

* build(deps): bump mysql-connector-python to 9.1.0

Fixes GHSA-hgjp-83m4-h4fj, a connector takeover vulnerability.

mysql test-requirements-1.txt moves from 9.0.0 to 9.1.0, which steps one
minor past the ~=9.0.0 that tox.ini records for that environment, and
docs-requirements.txt moves from ~=8.0 to ~=9.1.

Two files keep an 8.x pin. mysql test-requirements-0.txt is the 8.x entry
of the matrix tox.ini documents, and the fix is first available in 9.1.0.
The docker tests keep 8.3.0 because 9.1.0 makes five sqlalchemy tests in
sqlalchemy_tests/test_mysql.py fail: the span name drops to SELECT from
SELECT opentelemetry-tests, so the database name is no longer reaching
the span. That is a behaviour change in the instrumentation rather than a
stale expectation, so it needs its own investigation.

Fixes GHSA-v4x9-3549-crwv (heap out-of-bounds write via signed size
overflow in BSON document encoding), GHSA-vp6j-j7w5-5xjj (host injection
in connection string parsing), GHSA-qx36-8mw2-4r3x (forced Unix domain
socket connection via a .sock KMS endpoint) and GHSA-8fvv-fgr5-f8ch
(inexact file ID match in GridFS delete methods).

dnspython moves because pymongo 4.18.2 requires it.

* build(deps): widen starlette to ~=1.3.1 in docs-requirements

Fixes GHSA-82w8-qh3p-5jfq (request.form() limits silently ignored for
application/x-www-form-urlencoded), GHSA-wqp7-x3pw-xc5r (SSRF and NTLM
credential theft via UNC paths in StaticFiles) and the remaining open
starlette advisories, none of which has a fix inside the ~=0.50 range
this file pinned.

* build(deps): bump the vulnerable pins in the uv-generated test requirements

Covers anyio 4.14.2 (GHSA-82r6-8w77-94w6, GHSA-3w57-8xmc-8v26,
GHSA-5p39-cfhj-2xmp), urllib3 2.8.0 (GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77 and the rest of
the open urllib3 set), kafka-python 2.3.2 (GHSA-2jcm-hq8r-84wx and
GHSA-m3px-q5gj-j9x7) and multidict 6.9.1 (GHSA-54p9-h82j-f925).

The matching floors in the test-requirements.in files move with them, so
a later regeneration cannot drop back below a fix.

These files are edited in place rather than regenerated. Regenerating
fastapi test-requirements.latest.txt from its current .in file replaces
fastapi 0.137.2 with 0.119.1 and starlette 1.3.1 with 0.48.0, because
the .in file still asks for fastapi~=0.119.1. That would reintroduce the
starlette advisories this PR is clearing, so the generated files have
been left otherwise untouched.

fastapi test-requirements.oldest.txt keeps starlette 0.48.0. It pins
fastapi 0.119.1, which requires starlette<0.49.0, and the first starlette
fix is 0.49.1.
